{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint lacks a stated statistical analysis",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint is ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint is defined but no statistical analysis method (e.g., exact binomial confidence interval, hypothesis test) is described in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the analysis for the primary endpoint, including the estimator, confidence interval method, and any hypothesis testing."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint 'Response in injected and noninjected target lesions' has no analysis",
      "quote": "Response in injected and noninjected target lesions per RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This secondary endpoint is listed but no analysis is described in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Specify the analysis for this endpoint, including how response in injected and noninjected lesions will be summarized and compared."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety endpoint lacks a stated analysis",
      "quote": "AEs, SAEs, and AEs leading to discontinuation or death, and severity of AEs as assessed by the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events Version 5.0 (CTCAE v5.0)",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is defined but the statistical methods section only lists safety assessments without specifying how AEs will be analyzed (e.g., incidence rates, severity summaries).",
      "fix": "Add a detailed safety analysis plan, including how TEAEs will be summarized and any statistical comparisons."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on RECIST v1.1.",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The estimand for the primary endpoint is incomplete: it lacks specification of the population (e.g., all treated subjects), the handling of intercurrent events (e.g., treatment discontinuation, death), and the summary measure (e.g., proportion with exact confidence interval).",
      "fix": "Define the estimand attributes for the primary endpoint, including population, variable, intercurrent events strategy, and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size justification lacks statistical inputs",
      "quote": "The total number of subjects to be enrolled into this study is approximately 225.",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification does not provide alpha, power, or effect size inputs. It only lists expected ORRs and confidence interval lower bounds, but no formal calculation basis.",
      "fix": "Provide the statistical assumptions (alpha, power, target effect size) used to derive the sample size of 225."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent sample size across cohorts",
      "quote": "Each cohort of A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D, E, and F, will enroll approximately 25 subjects. The total number of subjects to be enrolled into this study is approximately 225.",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The text states each of 9 cohorts will enroll approximately 25 subjects, which sums to 225, but the phrase 'approximately' introduces ambiguity. Also, the table lists 9 cohorts, but the text says 'Cohorts A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D, E, and F' which is consistent, but the total is approximate.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the total is fixed at 225 or may vary, and ensure consistency between per-cohort and total numbers."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "Categorical variables will be summarized as the number and percentage of subjects within each category (with a category for missing data, if applicable).",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The general considerations mention a category for missing data for categorical variables, but there is no overall strategy for handling missing data in efficacy analyses (e.g., how missing responses are handled in ORR, PFS, OS).",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling for all endpoints, including sensitivity analyses if needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "No multiplicity adjustment for multiple cohorts and endpoints",
      "quote": "All efficacy endpoints will be summarized by cohort.",
      "page": 93,
      "section": "8.6",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The study evaluates multiple cohorts and multiple endpoints, but no multiplicity adjustment is described. This could lead to inflated type I error if any formal testing is done.",
      "fix": "Specify whether multiplicity adjustments are needed and, if so, describe the method (e.g., Bonferroni, hierarchical testing)."
    }
  ]
}
